references.role: Editorial pacing, photographic layering and restrained palette

assets.intended_use: Gallery chapter illustration matching the existing oxblood engravings
assets.prompt: Create ONE production-ready isolated website asset for an ACM-W student chapter's elegant archival correspondence website. Art direction: refined antique photographic archive meets scientific editorial, warm ivory #fff9e9, dark oxblood #580a0a, restrained oat and aged brass. Tactile and believable, not cute, not grunge, not kitsch. Orthographic flatbed/top-down view, no perspective tilt, no background, no scene, no props, no text, no watermark. Object fully visible with clear transparent margins on every side. An original late-19th-century wood-engraving style illustration of a single antique folding bellows camera viewed in restrained three-quarter profile, rectangular bellows body with extended lens, fine crosshatched lines and etched detail. Exactly one dark burgundy oxblood ink color #580a0a and transparent negative space. Dense enough to read at 180px yet delicate line variation. No photographic shading, no grey filled background, no labels, no tripod, no flowers, no frame. Match antique scientific plate engravings and letterpress stationery. Camera should fill most of square composition with airy outer transparent margin.

assets.intended_use: Women in STEM or research-focused editorial passage
assets.prompt: Create one isolated editorial illustration for a sophisticated ACM-W women-in-technology website. Subject: an elegant antique laboratory microscope in side three-quarter view, one complete instrument with eyepiece, objective, circular stage, focusing wheel and stable horseshoe foot. Style: original fine copperplate engraving, precise sparse cross-hatching and tapered ink strokes, monochrome deep burgundy #580a0a with genuinely transparent negative space and transparent background. Match vintage scientific publication plates. Restrained intellectual editorial aesthetic, clear silhouette that reads at 200px. Delicate rather than overly ornate. All highlights and open spaces between lines are transparent, not filled cream. Keep entire instrument within central 76% of the canvas, generous margins all sides. No surface, no photographic shading, no paper, no frame, no labels, no flowers, no tape, no scrapbook collage, no ornaments, no text, no logos. One illustration only.
